name: Aggressive Encroachment
summary: At the village, starving ursera now threaten the settlement. Valreaa Valewind calls for a cull after one beast nearly attacked a child at the elder tree.

sections.title: Desperate Predators
sections.body: Ursera from dens southwest of the village have become dangerous to its people. A hungry adolescent reached the base of the central elder tree and nearly mauled a child at play. The settlement's rangers killed the beast before anyone was hurt.

sections.title: Culling the Grove
sections.body: The rangers believe hunger is driving ursera toward settled ground. They have ordered a cull of the scrawniest beasts prowling outside their dens in Thendal Grove. The Rangers of the Grove hope this will stop further incursions while they seek the cause of the wildlife's distress.

faq.answer: Valreaa Valewind, a leader among the rangers, offers the work. She watches over the grove and protects the nearby settlement from predatory beasts.

faq.q: Why are the ursera wandering so close to the village?
faq.answer: The ursera are starving and desperate. Hunger drives them far beyond their usual hunting grounds and into the settlement.

faq.q: Where can the scrawny ursera be found?
faq.answer: Scrawny ursera prowl Thendal Grove southwest of the village, outside the den entrances rather than deep in the cave.
An adolescent ursera reached the elder tree in the middle of the village and tried to attack a young boy at play. Rangers killed the beast just in time to save him.

faq.q: Why are the ursera behaving so erratically?
faq.answer: The ursera have grown unusually aggressive, but the rangers do not know what caused their food shortage or change in behavior.

faq.q: What proof does Valreaa Valewind require?
faq.answer: Valreaa Valewind asks for six Scrawny Ursera Claws from the malnourished beasts prowling the grove, proof that the dangerous predators have been dealt with.

angles.text: As a hunter, you know starving predators may abandon their natural wariness of settlements when famine drives them.
As a druid, you can see the grove's balance shifting. The ursera's sudden aggression and malnutrition point to an unseen disturbance in the local ecosystem.
